event: Elsie wakes in the attic in the dark before dawn, and thinks of Ines's favourite hour.
She lies listening to the quiet: the canal slapping, a far-off boat, nobody else awake.
She whispers to Moonpenny that this is Ines's hour, and that it is rather nice, actually.
On the sill the two grey gloves lie side by side, the second one's thumb half grown.
She knits by the round window till the sky goes grey, and the thumb is done.
Downstairs Agnes is at the oven; the honey cakes still sit on the blue plate, all of them.
Elsie looks at the full plate a moment, and leaves it where it is.
She asks Agnes for a little crock of honey, and pays her three pips for it.

changes.note: Elsie buys a little crock of honey from Agnes for Ines: 3 pips, 211 → 208

event: Agnes ties a square of cloth over the crock's mouth with string, and asks who it's for.
Elsie says a girl who likes hot milk with honey and the hour before dawn.
Agnes adds a second knot to the string, and hands her a heel of yesterday's loaf for her breakfast.
The guild hall opens at seven; Ines is already at the clerk's desk, small in her black lace.
Around her there is a clear space on the boards, the way there is round Noor's table.
Two adventurers waiting behind her have stepped back a full pace, and whisper.
Elsie goes straight up and says good morning, and stands beside her, close.
Ines whispers to the clerk that Biscuit is home, found on the dome, by these ones.
The clerk unlocks the iron box and counts out two silver lanterns onto the desk.

changes.note: Elsie gains 30 XP for the F-rank Biscuit notice (30 → 60 / 350)
Tamsin gains 30 XP for the F-rank Biscuit notice (500 → 530)
Tilly gains 30 XP for the F-rank Biscuit notice (180 → 210 / 350)

event: Tamsin, Tilly and Cora come in together; Tilly is yawning, her book under her arm.
Tilly says she read about raising all night and has forty questions, and yawns again.
Elsie says the two lanterns should go whole to Margery's whetstone, if nobody minds.
Tilly says yes at once; Tamsin stares at the coins, then at Elsie, and goes red.
Elsie puts both lanterns into Tamsin's big hand and folds her fingers shut over them.

changes.note: Biscuit notice's 2 lanterns go whole to Tamsin for Margery's whetstone: 226 → 246
Bond: Tamsin 85 → 86 (kindness: the cat lanterns for Margery's whetstone)
Strength 18 → 19 (Devotion: Tamsin 86% of 21)
Tamsin Strength 38 → 39 (Devotion: 86% of 21)

event: Tamsin says gruffly that Margery says thank you, and pats the axe on her back.
Elsie gives Ines the little crock of honey, for her milk, as she promised.
Ines holds it in both hands against her lace and looks at it as if it were a bird.
She whispers that nobody has ever kept a promise to her so quickly.
Tilly asks Ines if she may come and ask her forty questions; Ines whispers yes, today.
Cora watches Ines from by the desk, ledger shut under her arm, her face unreadable.
Cora says to Ines, formally, that Biscuit's return will be noted as a found cat, nothing else.
Ines looks at Cora's coat a long moment, and whispers, Thank you, Warden.
Elsie takes Ines's free hand and leads her across the bare boards to Noor's table.

changes.note: Bond: Ines 5 → 7 (stand: Elsie leads her by the hand across the bare boards)

event: Noor watches them come, two of them now, and puts her coffee down.
Elsie says brightly, Noor, it's tomorrow, and sits on the good chair, after knocking twice.
Noor looks at Ines; Ines looks at Noor's gloves; neither looks away first.
Noor says dryly that people cross the street from her too, so Ines needn't sit too close.
Ines whispers that she doesn't mind bad luck, and sits down right beside her.
Nothing falls, spills or snaps; Noor looks almost put out about it.
Elsie asks Noor, as if it's simple: will you have lunch with me today?
Noor turns her cup a quarter turn, and another, and says: One o'clock. The Crooked Kettle.

changes.note: Bond: Noor 4 → 5 (kindness: asked to lunch once more, and she says yes)

event: She adds that she won't wait, so Elsie had better not be late.
Elsie squeals and claps, and Noor's spoon jumps out of her saucer onto the floor.
Noor looks at the spoon on the floor, and the corner of her mouth goes in hard.
Tilly takes Ines off toward Ash Lane, already asking how a mouse is raised.
Tamsin finds a cutler on Brightwater Square and pays one lantern for a good grey whetstone.

changes.note: Tamsin pays one lantern for a grey whetstone: 246 → 236

event: She sits on the canal steps with Margery across her knees and works the edge, long strokes.
The stone rings on the steel; Tamsin hums along with it without knowing, like Elsie does.
Elsie sits on the step above her and knits the first finger of the second glove.
Cora stands at the top of the steps; Elsie pats the step beside her until Cora sits.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 53 → 54 (kindness: Elsie pats the step until she sits)

event: Tamsin holds Margery up to the light; the edge shines thin and bright along its curve.
She shaves a hair off her own arm with it, and grins up at Elsie, wide and crooked.
Tamsin says let's go and look at the house, just look, just to say good morning to it.
On Willow Canal the blue door stands open, and voices come out of the house.
In the wild garden the Coin Street agent is showing four adventurers round.
They are a C-rank party in good leather, and one of them is measuring the front window.
Tamsin stops dead at the gate with her hand on Margery's strap.
The agent comes out and says, not unkindly, that it's still whoever brings four suns first.
The C-rank party says loudly that they'll have the gold after their Midsummer job.
Elsie looks up at the house: the three storeys, the sills, the garden gone to seed.
Tamsin counts on her fingers with her lips moving, then counts again.
She says, flat, that with Tilly's purse too they're about eight lanterns short.
Elsie says eight lanterns isn't so very many, and her voice comes out smaller than she meant.
She presses two fingers to the blue door frame as they pass, and so does Tamsin.
Cora watches them both do it, and looks at the door a long moment herself.
Back at the guild hall, Tamsin goes straight down the E-rank board, reading fast.
She stops at one notice and taps it: guard the Midsummer barges from river thieves, twelve lanterns.
Elsie reads it: dusk to dawn on the twentieth, from boats the festival lends.
Twelve lanterns, Tamsin says. Eight for the house, and four left over for pie.
Cora says, very evenly, that thieves on Midsummer night carry knives, not cream bowls.
Elsie says they'll be careful, and that Cora will be in the boat, so they'll be safe.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 54 → 56 (stand: with Cora in the boat they'll be safe)

event: Cora looks at her, and says nothing, and doesn't argue again.
Elsie signs for the party at the clerk's desk; the clerk stamps it for the twentieth.
Tamsin says the whole city will be out on the Mere, and Celestine Okafor will sing on the barge.
Elsie says slowly that Celestine Okafor is Amara's mother.
Elsie thinks of Amara on the barrow in the dark, who can't sing if anyone is listening.
She doesn't say anything else, and goes quiet with the notice in her hand.
Tamsin goes off to the docks to tell her mum about the barges, Margery shining on her back.
Elsie and Cora walk through Lantern Square, where a field of bronze threads stands.
The threads are hundreds of thin bronze rods, each cut through near the top, each with a name.
Elsie asks what it is; Cora says the Memorial of Strings, for the war's dead.
Cora walks into the rows without seeming to decide to, and stops before five threads together.
Five names on five cut threads, all Vane, and fresh wax on the stone beneath them.
Cora says, in her report voice, that they were her grandmother's parents and her three brothers.
She says her grandmother lives on this square and lights five candles every night.
Elsie doesn't say anything at first; she looks at the five names a long time.
She takes Cora's bare hand, quite simply, and holds it, and they stand there together.

changes.note: Bond: Cora 56 → 58 (held through grief at the five threads; cut to the cap of 5)
Heart 18 → 19 (Devotion: Cora 58% of 21)
Cora Heart 32 → 33 (Devotion: 58% of 21)

event: Cora doesn't take her hand back; her fingers close, slowly, round Elsie's.
Elsie says quietly she understands now why Cora said, Don't do that again.
Cora says that isn't why, and stops, and doesn't say what is.
From a tall house on the square, through a high open window, comes a girl's voice singing.
It is low and warm and wandering, and Elsie knows it at once from the barrow.
Elsie looks up; the singing stops dead in the middle of a note.
A face with long braids is at the window for a heartbeat, then the curtain swings shut.
Elsie lets her breath go and says softly that it's Amara, and she doesn't wave.
She says to Cora that they shouldn't stand and listen, and walks on, still holding her hand.
At the Crooked Kettle Noor is already at a corner table, alone, at five to one.
Cora takes the table by the door, orders a pot of tea, and opens her ledger.
Noor looks at Cora by the door, and at Elsie, and says, You brought your Warden.
Elsie says Cora goes everywhere, she can't help it, and she likes quiet, so she won't talk.
They have leek soup and brown bread; Noor eats with her gloves on, neatly.
A gust through the door lifts Elsie's napkin into the soup; she fishes it out, laughing.
The waiter trips on nothing beside them and saves the teapot by a whisker.
Elsie's flower clip slides out of her hair and drops into the bread basket.

changes.note: Elsie's flower clip slides out of her hair into the bread basket

event: Noor says flatly that this is why she eats alone, and puts down her spoon.
Elsie says it's the best lunch she's had in Lanternmere, and means it.
Noor looks at her across the table a long time, then fishes the clip out of the bread.
She clips it back into Elsie's hair with her gloved fingers, careful, and sits back.

changes.note: Noor clips the flower clip back into Elsie's hair

event: Elsie asks Noor if she'll come out on the Mere with them on Midsummer, guarding barges.
She says they'd love a fourth, and Noor needn't sit near anyone if she'd rather not.

changes.note: Bond: Noor 5 → 7 (stand: asked into the party's boat for Midsummer)

event: Noor stares at her, and says, quite quietly, that boats sink round her.
Elsie says then they'll take Tilly's floating vials, and Tamsin swims like a fish.
Noor turns her cup a full turn on the table, and says: Ask me tomorrow.
Elsie laughs out loud and says that's what she said yesterday, and look what happened.
Noor puts down coins for both their lunches before Elsie can open her purse.
At the door Cora's ledger lies open; the page reads: Lunch. Skills used, none.
Elsie walks Cora back to the guild hall along the canals in the long afternoon.
Elsie knits as she walks; the glove's first finger grows past the length of her own.
Cora watches the needles and asks, at last, low, whose fingers it's measured for.
Elsie says it's still a surprise, and Cora looks down at her own long fingers on the ledger.
At six the guild hall shuts; Cora stops on the top step, where she goes off duty.
She says, Fairweather, and inclines her head, and then doesn't go.
She says she'll be at the Lantern Steps at dusk on the twentieth, with her lantern.
Elsie says she knows, and hugs her quickly round the middle, coat, ledger and all.
Cora stands stiff in it, then her hand rests a moment on Elsie's back, and lifts.
Cora goes off along the canal toward Wick Lane, and looks back at the second bridge.
In the attic Elsie knits the glove's second finger by the round window as the lanterns light.
Below on Thimble Canal, under the red lantern, a girl with long braids stops at the window.
She stands looking at the honey cakes a long while, as she did before, and turns to go.
Elsie drops her knitting and runs down the attic stair and through the dark shop.
She opens the shop door; Amara is three steps off along the canal walk, and stops.
Elsie says, Hello, Amara, they're for you, they've always been for you, come in.
Amara laughs, startled, and says she's walked past three times now.
Elsie says she knows, and fetches the blue plate out of the window, and they sit on the step.
Amara eats a honey cake slowly with her eyes shut, and licks honey off her thumb.
She says it's better than the barrow, and Elsie claps, quietly, because it's late.
Amara asks, not looking at her, whether Elsie heard her singing this morning on the square.
Elsie says yes, a little, but she walked on, because she didn't think Amara wanted her to stay.
Amara turns the cake in her fingers and says nobody has ever walked on before.
She says her mother wants her to sing beside her on the barge on Midsummer night.
She says she hasn't told her mother she can't sing a note with anyone listening.
Elsie says that sounds like the heaviest thing she's ever heard anyone carry.
She puts her arm round Amara's shoulders and leaves it there, warm, on the step.

changes.note: Bond: Amara 2 → 5 (held through a fear: the Midsummer song, an arm round her)

event: Amara leans into her side by inches, and rests her head on Elsie's shoulder.
Elsie says she'll be out on the dark water that night guarding barges, not listening.
She says if Amara looks for a boat with a pink head in it, that'll be her, not listening at all.
Amara laughs into her shoulder, a wet sort of laugh, and doesn't lift her head for a while.
Elsie wraps the rest of the cakes in paper and puts them in Amara's hands to take home.
Amara stands, holding the parcel, and says, You're the Enthraller, aren't you, quite softly.
Elsie says yes, and that it's a dreadful name, and she'd have picked one with flowers in.
Amara laughs again, says goodnight, and walks off under the lanterns, looking back twice.
Up in the attic Elsie writes in Noor's page: lunch, yes! and in Amara's: home, ate three.
She draws a little boat on the Midsummer page, with a lantern in it and five heads.
She looks at it, and adds a sixth head with braids, small, at the very back, and rubs it out.
She tells Moonpenny about the bronze threads, and the singing, and the blue door, and Noor's yes.
She lays the second glove by the first, two fingers done now, and blows out the candle.
